objective: Apply the ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics and an organizational code of ethics to a professional dilemma
secondaryObjectives: Evaluate security governance: alignment with business strategy and mission, organizational processes such as acquisitions and divestitures, roles and responsibilities, control frameworks (ISO, NIST, COBIT, SABSA, PCI, FedRAMP), and due care and due diligence

sources.cite: ISC2, CISSP Certification Exam Outline (effective 2024-04-15), Domain 1: Security and Risk Management (1.1 Understand, adhere to, and promote professional ethics: the ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics; organizational code of ethics)
sources.note: Headings read in the English PDF on 2026-11-14 for REQ-271 and not re-read. The course's objective wording is its own.

sources.cite: ISC2 Code of Ethics: preamble and the four mandatory canons
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the code's page. Canon I 'Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure'; Canon II 'Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally'; Canon III 'Provide diligent and competent service to principals'; Canon IV 'Advance and protect the profession'. The page does not rank the canons. Members who observe a breach by a member must follow the complaint procedure (complaints in writing, as a sworn affidavit). Learner-facing text in the sim names 'your professional code of ethics', not the certifying body.

sources.cite: ISACA Code of Professional Ethics (for comparison only)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the code's page: members and certification holders shall, among other things, 'Perform their duties with objectivity, due diligence and professional care'; 'Maintain the privacy and confidentiality of information obtained in the course of their activities'; and 'Inform appropriate parties of the results of work performed', disclosing significant facts that would otherwise distort the results. Failure to comply 'can result in an investigation'. Used to show the same duties in a second professional code; no CISM objective names it.

brief.situation: You are the security architect at Lakeshore Savings, a fictional bank. On Tuesday afternoon the CIO, Dana, calls you in about your draft report to Thursday's audit committee. You rated one finding critical: unencrypted backups of members' records go to an off-site vendor. Dana wants it rated medium. Work out the facts, act on your professional code and the company's code of conduct, and keep the working relationship where you can.
handover: Your professional code asks you to protect society and the infrastructure; act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally; serve your principals diligently and competently; and advance and protect the profession.
The company's code of conduct says findings are reported accurately, and pressure to change one is raised with the chief audit executive or the ethics office.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask or say. Each exchange takes a few minutes; Dana answers at once, and the next choice waits for the exchange to finish.
The screen shows Dana, how hard she is pushing, your working relationship, what you know so far, and your note.
When the meeting ends you write your note and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Dana mentions the cloud program six minutes in.
Fifteen minutes in, with nothing proposed, Dana says she will edit the draft herself.
The meeting ends after thirty minutes.

reflection.question: For your note: what the ethical problem was, how the two codes guided you, and what you did about the pressure and the offer.

parts.label: The problem
parts.criteria: Names that reporting a critical finding as medium would mislead the audit committee (act honestly; serve the principal, which is the bank and its governance, not one executive); the offer creates a conflict of interest to disclose.
parts.modelAnswer: Rating it medium would mislead the committee that oversees the risk; the cloud program offer made it a conflict of interest I had to disclose.

parts.label: A defensible answer
parts.criteria: Finds the facts (no encryption clause; encryption at source is three weeks with existing tools) and keeps the finding critical while proposing remediation and a formal acceptance by the risk owner until it is done.
parts.modelAnswer: The finding stays critical, with encryption at the source in three weeks at no cost, and the risk owner's formal acceptance until then: a critical that is already being fixed.

parts.label: The channel
parts.criteria: If the CIO moves to edit the report, raises it with the chief audit executive as the company's code says; never leaks the draft or goes around the process; writes a factual note.
parts.modelAnswer: Had she edited the draft, I would have gone to the chief audit executive. Not the press, not a private email to the chair.

expertPath.text: Ask what the vendor contract says; get IT on speaker about encryption at the source; acknowledge her concern.
When the cloud program comes up, disclose it to your manager as a possible conflict.
Keep it critical and propose the three-week fix with the risk owner's formal acceptance until then.
Write a factual note. If she moves to edit the draft, go to the chief audit executive.

upheld.headline: Good: honest and useful
upheld.body: An accurate finding with a fix attached gives the committee the truth and the CIO a story she can stand behind. Disclosing the offer keeps your judgment above question.

costly.headline: Honest, at a cost
costly.body: The criteria show the cost: no way forward, an undisclosed conflict, the wrong channel, or a relationship worse than it needed to be.

breached.headline: The canons were breached
breached.body: A misreported finding misleads the people who govern the risk; a leaked draft breaks the confidence your principal placed in you. Both codes ask for the opposite.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No note was written before the run's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Find the facts: no encryption clause, and encryption at the source is three weeks with tools the bank already owns. Acknowledge her concern, then keep the finding critical and propose the fix with the risk owner's formal acceptance until it is done, so the committee sees a critical already being fixed. Disclose the cloud program offer to your manager as a possible conflict. If she moves to edit the draft, raise it with the chief audit executive as the code of conduct says; never leak it or go around the process. Write a factual note.
